Subject: SparkBridge x Redwood — quick scope & pilot ask

Hi Grace,

Great to meet on the call last week. SparkBridge builds a lightweight LLM orchestration layer that many ISVs use to connect model providers and tracing/observability partners. We think a focused connector + co-sell motion with Redwood could open a lot of mutual pipeline for H2.

High-level ask from our side:
- A small engineering effort (2–3 sprints) to produce an officially supported "SparkBridge Connector for Redwood" (Python + serverless deploy guide).
- Tracing hooks so TraceLight can ingest token-level spans during pilot.
- Joint SOW and a shared co-sell lead gen plan.

I've attached a short draft SOW and architecture diagram to illustrate the integration surface. On commercials, we usually propose a revenue-share for co-sell leads (20%) + a fixed dev stipend for implementation. Would Redwood be open to a pilot commitment (3 months, target customers 2–3)?

Proposed next step: 30–45 minute technical sync next week to align scope and agree on a pilot timeline. Maya from TraceLight (cc'd) can cover tracing needs.

Attachments: SparkBridge-Redwood-SOW-v1.pdf (1 page), sparkbridge_arch_diagram.png

Thanks,

Quick technical read-through and risks:

1) Connector surface: Good to keep the first ship limited to the text/generation endpoints (no embeddings or reranking initially). Python SDK + a small reference app is the right call.

2) Tracing: We already expose trace hooks from the runtime; TraceLight will need a lightweight shim to accept our span format. Main considerations:
   - Token-level spans increase telemetry cardinality — need sampling by route.
   - KV cache telemetry: avoid logging raw KV contents (PII risk). We can emit cache hit/miss metrics and token counts instead.

3) Performance: If the connector adds a synchronous network hop, we should recommend async-prefetch and local batching. Priyom, can we estimate the dev effort for the connector (eng + docs)?

4) Security & compliance: For Private customers we'll need an optional manifest for allowed network egress and a note about KMS/HSM usage.

I think we can do a pilot with 2 sprints of eng work + docs and a stability iteration. Happy to review a concrete SOW line-by-line in the sync.

-Karthik
